title: SRE weekly roundup + on-call handoff (Apr 02 2026)
content:
Weekly SRE roundup — notes for the team, on-call handoff details, and action items.

Context / TL;DR
- Busy week: two Sev2 incidents (tail-latency spikes for hosted text-generation, and a misfiring autoscaler that caused throttled Dedicated workers).
- SLO standing: overall 99.95% for API availability last 7d, but request latency SLOs dipped in a few regions during spikes.
- Runbook: updated the kv-cache failover steps and added a diagnostic checklist for batcher backpressure.
- Handoff: Maya -> Arjun for on-call week (Apr 02–Apr 09). Primary Slack channel: #sre-oncall; escalation: Lina (pager), Evan (pager).

Incidents this week
1) Incident RI-2689: Hosted API tail-latency spike (2026-03-30 02:10–02:46 UTC) — Sev2
   - Symptom: 99th/99.9th percentile token-generation latency increased ~4-7x across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for ~36 minutes. Error rates did not meaningfully change (5xx stayed <0.1%).
   - Root cause hypothesis: A recent gateway change (connection pooling tweak rolled Mar 29) interacted poorly with TTL-based prefix cache invalidation; resulted in frequent cold KV cache misses + repeated backend warmups, causing CPU/latency tail.
   - Mitigation performed: Rolled back gateway pooling change + enabled emergency kv-cache-prewarm for high-traffic model profiles (hotfix script). Latency returned to normal within ~8 minutes after rollback.
   - Postmortem status: Draft started; assigned to Lina (owner). Action item: add an automated canary that exercises head-of-queue long-tail scenarios.

2) Autoscaler misfire — Dedicated worker pool (2026-03-31 18:22–19:05 UTC) — Sev3 -> tracked for capacity commit
   - Symptom: Autoscaler erroneously restrained scale-up during transient GC events on nodes running the scheduling controller; spike in queue length and 429s for queued Dedicated requests at ~18:30 UTC.
   - Root cause: Scheduling controller pod was OOMing on a specific controller loop due to an inefficient metadata listing query.
   - Mitigation: Emergency patch to reduce list window, bumped node pool by +2 GPUs to absorb backlog, and patched controller to page listings.
   - Follow-ups: Performance test for controller under large customer counts; create a Synthetic / soak test in staging that mimics Dedicated peak profile. Owner: Evan.

SLOs and metrics
- Availability SLO (hosted API): 99.95% rolling 30d — current 30d: 99.97%, 7d: 99.95% (brief dips during RI-2689).
- Latency SLO (p50/p95/p99 generation latency for short prompts): target p95 < 120ms, p99 < 350ms.
  - Last 7d p95: 115ms (OK), p99: 410ms (miss) — driven by the Mar 30 tail events in two regions.
- Error budget burn: We consumed ~12% of monthly error budget for latency SLOs this week.
- Alert noise: High page volume from "BatcherBackpressure" alerts at odd hours — investigating tuning thresholds.

On-call handoff notes (Maya -> Arjun)
- Coverage window: starting 2026-04-02 18:00 UTC handoff call, Arjun primary til 2026-04-09 18:00 UTC.
- Escalation order: Arjun (primary), Lina (pager 1), Evan (pager 2), Maya (fallback).
- Known at-handoff issues: RI-2689 postmortem in draft; kv-cache prewarm script is in scripts/ops/kv_prewarm.sh (be cautious — requires run_as infra-admin). The autoscaler controller patch is in staging; do not promote until load-test green.
- Runbook pointers:
  - kv-cache failover: confluence link in metadata + runbook step numbers at top of page.
  - Batcher diagnostics: /runbooks/batcher-diagnostics.md — added new section on observing queue depth and pending-batches metric.
- Pager etiquette reminders: when you page Lina, add "[PAGER] brief context + region + first 3 logs" to reduce ping cycles.

Runbook and tooling updates
- Added "kv-cache-prewarm" step with automated prewarm job (PR #1024) — description and parameters included in the runbook.
- Batcher backpressure: added explicit thresholds and a safe autoscaling backoff for the batcher controller.
- New daily healthcheck job (cron) to run a generation request pattern that mimics PLG traffic: runs at 02:00 UTC daily across us-east-1/us-west-2/eu-west-1. Will surface regressions early.
- Note: The new healthcheck requires a small API key with test-only quotas; key stored in Vault path secret/sre/healthcheck-key (team leads only).

Action items (tracked)
- Lina: Finish RI-2689 postmortem and add canary test to CI (owner; due 2026-04-06).
- Evan: Add staged soak test for Dedicated autoscaler; create load profile and runbook for scaling exercises (owner; due 2026-04-09).
- Arjun (incoming oncall): Verify daily healthchecks success and watch for noisy batcher alerts; tune thresholds if >3 false positives in 48h.
- Maya: Draft a short runbook checklist for emergent rollback of gateway changes (owner; due 2026-04-05).

Meeting notes — weekly SRE sync (2026-04-01)
- Agenda: incidents review, SLO burn, infra spend and Dedicated pool sizing, runbook priorities.
- Key decisions: prioritize canary coverage for gateway changes (must pass for any pooling/conn-change PR > small risk label).
- Budget note: infra spend for Dedicated GPUs trending +8% month-over-month; product ops to review committed capacity vs observed peak.
- Ops request: solutions-eng asked SRE to provide guidance on model cold-start expectations for customers using Dedicated vs Hosted — action Maya + Lina to draft one-pager.

Open questions / TODOs / notes to self
- Should we create a separate latency-SLO for tail (p99.9) given observed long-tail impact? Pros: better signal; Cons: extra noise and more aggressive alerts. Quick poll in #sre-offline.
- Follow up with infra-team on GC tuning on containers (seen some spikes that align with node restarts).
- Confirm runbook permissions for kv-prewarm (avoid accidental runs by non-admins).
- Add synthetic request for reranking endpoints (seen small degradation, not yet impacting SLOs).

Files / artifacts referenced this doc (local)
- scripts/ops/kv_prewarm.sh — needs review before we automate crons.
- infra/monitoring/alerts/batcher.yaml — proposed threshold changes in branch.
- confluence: kv-cache-fallbacks (link in metadata).

Handoff checklist (quick)
- [ ] Confirm Slack status + set custom status "oncall: Arjun (Apr2–Apr9)"
- [ ] Check PagerDuty schedule and confirm escalation policies (Lina/Evan pinned)
- [ ] Ensure daily healthcheck ran successfully this morning (02:00 UTC run)
- [ ] Read RI-2689 draft and note any outstanding telemetry needs

Quick reminders for incoming on-call
- Prioritize head-of-queue latency alerts; if p99 > 500ms for >10 min in multiple regions, escalate to Lina immediately.
- For autoscaler-related 429s, check the scheduling-controller logs (kubectl -n infra logs controller) and the controller-metrics dashboards (link in runbooks).
- Use the "emergency scale" playbook only when backlog cannot be drained within 15 minutes after initial mitigation.

If anything critical crops up over the weekend ping me (Maya) directly in Slack @maya.r — I'll be available for one urgent escalation only.

-- end of weekly roundup --

Notes: rough draft — will iterate post-hand off and after RI-2689 postmortem is finalized.
